name: Question 8
worked_solution:
The linearity property of the Laplace transform states that for functions $f(t)$ and $g(t),$ we have

$$
L{\alpha f(t)+\beta g(t)}=\alpha \cdot L{f(t)}+\beta \cdot L{g(t)}
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants.

First, we expand:

$$
f(t)=(4t+1)^{2}=16{t}^{2}+8t+1
$$

Taking the Laplace transform and applying the linearity properties, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{f(t)} & =L{16{t}^{2}+8t+1} \\  & =L{16{t}^{2}}+L{8t}+L{1} \\  & =16L{{t}^{2}}+8L{t}+L{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $L{{t}^{n}}=\frac{n!}{{s}^{n+1}}.$ Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{t}^{2}} & =\frac{2}{{s}^{3}},\,s>0 \\ L{t} & =\frac{1}{{s}^{2}},\,s>0 \\ L{1} & =\frac{1}{s},\,s>0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Laplace transform of $f(t)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L{f(t)} & =16L{{t}^{2}}+8L{t}+L{1} \\  & =16\cdot \frac{2}{{s}^{3}}+8\cdot \frac{1}{{s}^{2}}+\frac{1}{s} \\  & =\frac{32}{{s}^{3}}+\frac{8}{{s}^{2}}+\frac{1}{s} \\  & =\frac{{s}^{2}+8s+32}{{s}^{3}},\,s>0.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we expand:

f(t)=(4t+1)2=16t2+8t+1

Taking the Laplace transform and applying the linearity properties, we have

L{f(t)}=L{16t2+8t+1}=L{16t2}+L{8t}+L{1}=16L{t2}+8L{t}+L{1}.

We're given that L{tn}=n!sn+1. Therefore, we have the following: L{t2}=2s3,s>0L{t}=1s2,s>0L{1}=1s,s>0

Therefore, the Laplace transform of f(t) is L{f(t)}=16L{t2}+8L{t}+L{1}=16⋅2s3+8⋅1s2+1s=32s3+8s2+1s=s2+8s+32s3,s>0.
